cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: Greater Bengaluru Authority chief commissioner Maheshwar Rao has asked the five city corporations to speed up pothole repairs and penalise unauthorised digging on newly asphalted roads.

lead.headline: RETAIL INFLATION HITS 6.09%, BREACHING RBI’S UPPER BAND
lead.deck: October’s consumer inflation crossed 6% for the first time in two years as food prices climbed, intensifying pressure on household budgets and the central bank.
paragraphs: India’s retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September, and moved above the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years.

Food inflation accelerated to 8.94% from 7.74%. Onion prices rose 116.22% year on year and garlic 60.74%, according to provisional figures released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
The reading follows the change to the consumer price index series and may strengthen expectations of another rate increase. The RBI’s next policy decision is due in December.

sidebarStory.headline: OLA FINED ₹10 LAKH OVER ADVANCE-TIP PROMPTS
sidebarStory.subhead: The consumer regulator says the app misled riders by suggesting an advance tip could improve their chances of getting a quicker ride.
paragraphs: The Central Consumer Protection Authority directed ANI Technologies, which operates Ola, to stop the advance tipping prompt and imposed a ₹10-lakh penalty.
The authority said the prompt created a misleading impression that paying extra could speed up driver acceptance. Its order was issued on November 10.

stories.headline: BRIDE-TO-BE AND COUSIN KILLED IN CONTAINER-TRUCK CRASH
paragraphs: A woman due to marry later this month and her cousin died after a container truck hit their scooter in Bengaluru on Thursday.
The pair had been travelling to deliver a final wedding invitation, police said. The fatal collision has renewed attention on heavy vehicles and two-wheeler safety on the city’s roads.

stories.headline: GBA OFFICIAL, 32 OTHERS BOOKED OVER 98 E-KHATAS
paragraphs: An assistant commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority and 32 others have been booked for allegedly issuing digital property records for 98 ineligible properties.
The FIR says the e-khatas were issued between January and June despite rules barring papers for certain unauthorised properties.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA TO DRAFT QUANTUM TECHNOLOGY POLICY
paragraphs: The state plans a policy to support quantum research, education, startups and industry, minister Ajay Dharam Singh said.
Officials were also asked to prepare for Quantum India Bengaluru 2027, which the government hopes to develop as a global platform.

stories.headline: DRAFT VOTER ROLLS GROW 1–3% IN STATES AFTER REVISION
paragraphs: Draft electoral rolls published in the first round of post-SIR revisions show voter numbers rising by between 1% and 3% across the covered states and union territories.
The Election Commission said schedules for several remaining states, including Karnataka, would be announced later. The draft lists are open to claims and corrections.

stories.headline: 43 WOMEN RESCUED IN ALLEGED HYDERABAD EGG-HARVESTING RACKET
paragraphs: Police rescued 43 women in an alleged illegal egg-extraction and sale operation in Hyderabad and are investigating possible links to 23 IVF centres.
Eight suspects have been arrested. Investigators say some women were recruited through financial promises and are examining whether coercion or deception was involved.

stories.headline: RBI CONSOLIDATES RULES FOR DOMESTIC MONEY TRANSFERS
paragraphs: New RBI directions bring domestic money-transfer instructions for banks and authorised payment operators into a single framework, effective immediately.
The rules cover cash-based remittances, including services used by people without bank accounts, and require cash remittances to be identified in transaction messages.

stories.headline: RAMESHWARAM CAFE WARNS OF FAKE FRANCHISE OFFERS
paragraphs: The Bengaluru-founded restaurant chain has issued a public warning after fake franchise letters circulated using its name.
The company cautioned prospective partners against paying money in response to unauthorised offers. The chain has expanded beyond Karnataka to cities including Hyderabad, Pune and Mumbai.

stories.headline: NEW VANDE BHARAT TO LINK BENGALURU, MANGALURU AND MADGAON
paragraphs: A new Vande Bharat service is set to connect Bengaluru with Mangaluru and Madgaon, with regular operations scheduled to begin November 15.
The route adds a direct fast-train option between the state capital, the Karnataka coast and Goa; the existing Mangaluru–Madgaon Vande Bharat is due to be discontinued.

stories.headline: 45TH INDIA INTERNATIONAL TRADE FAIR OPENS TODAY
paragraphs: The 2026 India International Trade Fair opens at Bharat Mandapam, bringing more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad across 17 halls.
The fair runs through November 27. Public entry begins November 14; the first day is for business visitors.

stories.headline: INDIA BANS EXPORTS OF LITHIUM-ION BATTERY BLACK MASS
paragraphs: The government has prohibited exports of lithium-ion battery black mass, the material recovered when spent batteries and electronics are processed.
The change is intended to retain battery-recycling material for domestic processing as India builds its critical-minerals and cell-manufacturing capacity.

paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecasts partly cloudy skies for Bengaluru on Friday, with a minimum of 19°C and maximum of 29°C. No warning is in force.
